rules.statement: Make what the security policy says about how packages are published match the workflows in the repository: name only workflow files that exist, and don't claim trusted publishing or 'no long-lived API key' when a workflow pushes with a stored API key.
rules.why: A false supply-chain claim, or a reference to a workflow that isn't there, can lead consumers and auditors to skip checks because they think there is no stored key to steal.
rules.check: Compare the publishing paragraphs in SECURITY.md with .github/workflows: does every workflow it names exist, and does any job push with `--api-key` or a secret while the text claims trusted publishing or no API key?

rules.statement: Make every Markdown link to another document's section point at a heading that exists in that document, and make the target contain the content the link promises.
rules.why: A dead anchor lands the reader at the top of the file, and the promised content isn't there.
rules.check: For each `file.md#anchor` link added or changed, confirm the target file has a matching heading that contains the content the link describes.

rules.statement: Add a CHANGELOG entry when a change alters how the assembly version or assembly identity is computed, such as tying AssemblyVersion to the major version only.
rules.why: Consumers who use strong naming or binding redirects need to know that the assembly identity rule changed.
rules.check: Look for build props or targets that set AssemblyVersion, FileVersion or strong-naming properties, and confirm the Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md describes the change.

rules.statement: When a documentation catalog (for example of metrics, spans or meters) has no entries yet, say so in plain text under each table heading instead of leaving empty tables.
rules.why: Empty tables send readers to a catalog that tells them nothing.
rules.check: Look for Markdown tables in docs that have a header row but no data rows and no sentence saying nothing is defined yet.

rules.statement: Don't ask a pull request to hand-edit `.copier-answers.yml` or other files Copier generates to fix a mismatched answer; changes to those belong upstream in the project template.
rules.why: Copier writes and owns its answers file, so hand edits in a consuming repository are the wrong place for the fix.
rules.check: Before reporting a mismatch involving `.copier-answers.yml`, check whether the setting really comes from another template answer (for example package_license matching LICENSE.txt). If it does, don't ask for an edit to the answers file.

rules.statement: Don't report PublicAPI.Shipped.txt being filled outside a release when an already released library is adopting the public API analyzer and the entries match the surface of its last released version.
rules.why: The analyzer needs a baseline of the shipped surface to pass on an already released library, so this edit is a baseline record, not a release change.
rules.check: Check whether PublicAPI.Shipped.txt is being created or filled for the first time and whether the source matches the last release tag; if so, at most ask that the PR description call it a baseline.

rules.statement: Don't ask to remove a short, single-line CHANGELOG entry that records a project-template update just because it describes repository tooling.
rules.why: The maintainer keeps that one line so the tooling change stays visible in the project's history.
rules.check: If the tooling entry is one concise line and public API and behavior entries are kept separately, don't report it.
